images.title: Longer side, same angles
images.purpose: Show that a base of 5 cm and a base of 7 cm with the same two end angles give the same third angle.
images.composition: Two triangles side by side on a common bottom line, the smaller on the left and the larger on the right, with equal spacing and white space between.
exact_structure: Left triangle: base 5 cm, angle 60° at its left end, angle 70° at its right end, angle 50° at the top. Teal (#0072B2) outline with a light fill.

Right triangle: the same shape scaled up, base 7 cm (1.4 times as wide as the left base), angle 60° at its left end, angle 70° at its right end, angle 50° at the top. Amber (#E69F00) outline with a light fill.
Both bases lie on one shared horizontal grey (#6B7280) line, the 60° angle at the left end of each base.
The top angle (50°) of each triangle is marked with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc.
The 60° and 70° angles are small arcs in the triangle's own colour.
rejection: the two triangles having different angle values
the larger triangle not being the same shape as the smaller one
a base length other than 5 cm and 7 cm
images.takeaway: A longer base makes a bigger triangle but the third angle stays 50°.
images.description: Two triangles with angles 60°, 70° and 50°, one with a 5 cm base and a larger one with a 7 cm base.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to compare the purple top angles and notice they are equal.

image_decisions.why: The same two angles give the same third angle whatever the base length.
